title: On Inventing a lock no key could open
subtitle: 科技与创新 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科技与创新（人与社会·科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）
meta: 主题语境：科技与创新（人与社会·科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）　|　核心词汇：invent　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 invent 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the cook ① invented a lock no key could open before dawn, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② invents a lock no key could open in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ invent a lock no key could open at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ invented a lock no key could open before — a line in the menu for September 1982 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Inventing a lock no key could open before dawn, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ invent a whole set of reasons in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Invent a whole set of reasons at once and never mention it again.

By 1995 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ invents a whole set of reasons before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ invented a lock no key could open again when nobody else would.

⑩ To invent a lock no key could open, my mother said in 2000, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody invents a lock no key could open in public again and somebody must invent a lock no key could open before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 发明（一般过去式 invented a lock no key could open：1988 年厨子头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 发明（一般现在 invents a lock no key could open：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 发明（不定式 to invent a lock no key could open：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 发明（过去完成时 had invented a lock no key could open：1982 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 发明（动名词 inventing a lock no key could open 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 编造（invent a whole set of reasons：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去编造编出一整套理由）
G. v. 编造（invent a whole set of reasons：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 发明（后段两处：新来的客人照例 invents a whole set of reasons，而母亲又一次 invented a lock no key could open）

answers.why: invent 意为“发明”，1988 年厨子天没亮就发明发明一把没有钥匙能开的锁，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 invented。
invent 意为“发明”，自那以后厨子当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 invents。
invent 意为“发明”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯发明发明一把没有钥匙能开的锁”，此处为不定式 to invent a lock no key could open。
invent 意为“发明”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1995 年之前就有人发明过，故用过去完成时 had invented。
invent 意为“发明”，厨子说“发明发明一把没有钥匙能开的锁这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 inventing a lock no key could open 作主语。
invent 意为“编造”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去编造编出一整套理由”，should ever 之后用原形 invent a whole set of reasons。
invent 意为“编造”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻编造编出一整套理由（invent a whole set of reasons at once），以后再也不要提起。
invent 意为“发明”，新来的客人每个日子都照例编造编出一整套理由，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 invents。
invent 意为“发明”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就发明发明一把没有钥匙能开的锁，用一般过去式 invented 叙述。
invent 意为“发明”，结尾那句是母亲 2000 年的话：要发明发明一把没有钥匙能开的锁，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

多年以后，厨子仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（invents a lock no key could open）

老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻编造编出一整套理由，以后再也不要提起。（invent a whole set of reasons，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 invent 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1988 the cook invented a lock no key could open before dawn, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook invents a lock no key could open in public whenever the canteen asks.
Inventing a lock no key could open before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever invent a whole set of reasons in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen invents a whole set of reasons before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother invented a lock no key could open again, and the canteen remembered that half.
